items.definition: The band that goes around a dog's neck. It can hold a small tag with the dog's name.
items.example: Mum put Pip's name on his new collar.

items.definition: A strap you hold when you walk a dog, so the dog stays safe near traffic.
items.example: I hold the leash tightly at the crossing.

items.definition: Cleaning and brushing an animal's fur, nails and teeth to keep it healthy.
items.example: We brush the cat every week. That is grooming.

items.definition: A set of things you do in the same order every time. A bedtime routine helps your body get sleepy.
items.example: Our bedtime routine is the same every night.

items.definition: The soft clothes you wear in bed.
items.example: I put on my pyjamas before I brush my teeth.

items.definition: To clean your teeth with a toothbrush and toothpaste, usually for two minutes.
items.example: I brush my teeth before I put on my pyjamas.

items.definition: What you say to somebody when you go to bed. It is a wish for a deep sleep.
items.example: I say good night to my grandmother every night.

items.definition: A child who is in the same class as you. Classmates are the easiest people to be friends with.
items.example: Mai is my classmate, and she sits next to me.

items.definition: To say your name to somebody for the first time. It only means saying your name.
items.example: I introduced myself and said, I am An.

items.definition: To start playing with a group that is already playing. You ask first, and then you join in.
items.example: Can I join in your game?

items.definition: To do the same game with another child, side by side. It is the simplest friendship there is.
items.example: We play together at break time every day.

items.definition: A child you have just met. Saying hello twice makes a new child feel welcome.
items.example: I have a new friend in class 4B.

items.definition: The word you say when you meet somebody. You can use it all day long.
items.example: Hello, I am Minh.

items.definition: A short and casual way to say hello, used with people you already know.
items.example: Hi Bao, are you ready?

items.definition: A friendly question you ask after saying hello, to start a small talk.
items.example: Good morning! How are you today?

items.definition: The words you use to tell somebody your own name.
items.example: My name is Lan, and I am seven.

items.definition: What you say the first time you meet somebody. It is polite and warm.
items.example: Nice to meet you. I am Minh.

items.definition: The question word that asks for a thing or an idea. It is the most useful question word of all.
items.example: What does this word mean?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a person.
items.example: Who is your new teacher?

items.definition: Introduces the conditions on a and b.
items.example: ax + b = 0, where a is non-zero.

items.definition: At the time when something happens.
The question word that asks for a reason. Why questions are the most interesting ones.
items.example: Why do we have to sleep?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a way of doing something.
items.example: How do you spell your name?

items.definition: One of the ways your body finds out about the world. You have five main ones.
items.example: Smell is a sense that helps you find food.

items.definition: The screen at the back of your eye. Light lands on it and the picture begins.
items.example: The picture forms on the retina.

items.definition: The nerve that carries the picture from your eye to your brain.
items.example: The optic nerve carries the picture along to the brain.

items.definition: The little spiral inside your ear that turns vibrations into nerve signals.
items.example: The cochlea changes the movement of your eardrum into signals.

items.definition: The tiny bumps on your tongue that pick out sweet, salty, sour and bitter.
items.example: Taste buds tell you that the mango is sweet.

items.definition: The cable that carries messages inside your body, from the senses to the brain and back again.
items.example: A nerve carries the message from your finger to your brain.

items.definition: Not able to find the way home. If you are lost, you are not in trouble. You just need help.
items.example: Pip was lost, but he was not frightened of the dark.

items.definition: A smell that hangs in the air. Dogs can smell scents and follow them a long way.
items.example: Pip knew the scent of his own garden.

items.definition: What really happened, even when it is not the easy thing to say.
items.example: An told his mother the truth about the blue bowl.

items.definition: Saying something you know is not true, on purpose, to make things easier for yourself.
items.example: He could have said the wind broke the bowl, but that would be a lie.

items.definition: Something you say you will do. People remember a broken promise for a long time.
items.example: An promised to tell his mother everything from then on.

items.definition: Doing a calculation in your head, without a calculator and without paper.
items.example: Mental arithmetic gave me the rough figure, and the check gave me the right one.

items.definition: A rough number, close enough to show whether a real answer is possible.
items.example: Before you multiply, estimate: about 50 times about 30 is about 1500.

items.definition: Writing a number as the nearest convenient value, usually the nearest ten, hundred or thousand.
items.example: 47 rounds to 50, and 42 rounds to 40.

items.definition: The correction you add or subtract after you have rounded a number.
items.example: I rounded 19 up to 20, so the compensation is one lot of 24, and 480 − 24 = 456.

items.definition: To bear or transport something.
items.example: In 8 + 7 you write 5 and carry 1 to the next column.

items.definition: The part of a number that is left over when the division does not come out exactly.
items.example: 87 divided by 7 gives the quotient 12 and the remainder 3.
